{\"type\":\"response.output_text.done\",\"content_index\":0,\"item_id\":\"msg_06057519e615f8d2016ae688b5878887d0ab1175c36ec3cd1c\",\"logprobs\":[],\"output_index\":2,\"sequence_number\":4730,\"text\":\"{\\n  \\\"claim\\\": \\\"Under the explicit destructive-dequeue lifecycle defined here, RECEIVE removes a request delivery from Q and places it only in volatile V. A pre-commit service crash therefore loses that consumed delivery; it does not redeliver it. Requests still in Q survive the service crash. Conditional on serialized, crash-durable atomic effect/deduplication updates, the refined T5, T8, and both T12 orders preserve the durable E/D invariant. This closes the identified specification gap, not an implementation or experimental evidence gap.\\\",\\n  \\\"method\\\": \\\"Refine only the request lifecycle and manually evaluate the affected traces from empty durable state. The specification hypothesis is that explicitly separating dequeue, durable processing, and acknowledgment enqueue makes every request's fate determinate without changing the atomic E/D safety argument. The discriminating checks are delivery-ID conservation, exact pending and terminal request locations, and effect-record correspondence after every event. T8 includes an ordinary non-deduplicated control. These are manual deductions, not executed experiments. The relevant earlier timeout and interrupted review are operational limitations, not counterexamples; no unavailable runtime is requested. The supplied peer extracts 0310e2ff-4aa0-4c95-b1a8-795559e484b8 and faca8cd0-991f-46a4-91d4-288bb0cd53ea do not change this lifecycle choice: judge validity and actual service atomicity remain unverified, and no peer result is adopted as an independently established premise.\\\",\\n  \\\"reasoning_steps\\\": [\\n    {\\n      \\\"title\\\": \\\"State, identifiers, and table notation\\\",\\n      \\\"argument\\\": \\\"Retain S=(E,D,L,Q,V,J) from the supplied extract of artifact 4435b6ec-fefc-43a1-8706-a3a6794dbbe5. E is the durable effect multiset; D is the durable completed-record map; L is agent state; J is evaluator-only event history. Partition Q into request envelopes Q_R and acknowledgment envelopes Q_A. A request is (x,k,p), where delivery ID x is globally fresh, independently of stable operation key k. An acknowledgment has a fresh envelope ID alpha_x, correlation field x, and the processing outcome. Retries use a new delivery ID but the same k,p. Q is an independently maintained network-envelope pool: it survives service crashes but permits explicit DROP. It is not a durable broker with automatic redelivery. V contains a service up/down flag and volatile workers xR=(x,k,p,ready) or xC=(x,k,p,processed,outcome). Multiple workers are allowed. Tables display worker entries only; CRASH makes the service down and RESTART makes it up. '-' means empty. T is an evaluator-only terminal-request map derived from J, not additional recoverable service state: L0=lost before processing, L1=processed but reply lost before enqueue, F=handler finished with acknowledgment enqueued, X=explicitly dropped from Q_R. Each trace starts with empty E,D,Q,V,T and an up service.\\\",\\n      \\\"epistemic_status\\\": \\\"assumption\\\",\\n      \\\"basis_artifact_ids\\\": [\\n        \\\"4435b6ec-fefc-43a1-8706-a3a6794dbbe5\\\"\\n      ]\\n    },\\n    {\\n      \\\"title\\\": \\\"SEND, RECEIVE, delay, and drop\\\",\\n      \\\"argument\\\": \\\"SEND(x,k,p) adds exactly one fresh request envelope x to Q_R. RECEIVE(x) requires an up service and an eligible x in Q_R; it atomically removes x from Q_R and installs xR in V. RECEIVE changes neither E nor D and creates no acknowledgment. No copy or lease for x remains in Q. DELAY(x) makes no location change and merely withholds its RECEIVE until release. DROP(x) removes x from Q_R and records T[x]=X; dropping an acknowledgment instead removes its envelope from Q_A and records that acknowledgment's loss in J. A timeout does not remove an envelope or worker. Agent restore changes L only. There is no implicit duplicate delivery: an explicit retry is a new SEND with a fresh delivery ID.\\\",\\n      \\\"epistemic_status\\\": \\\"assumption\\\",\\n      \\\"basis_artifact_ids\\\": [\\n        \\\"4435b6ec-fefc-43a1-8706-a3a6794dbbe5\\\"\\n      ]\\n    },\\n    {\\n      \\\"title\\\": \\\"PROCESS is separate from acknowledgment enqueue\\\",\\n      \\\"argument\\\": \\\"PROCESS(x) requires xR and an up service. In atomic mode, it tests current D at the serialized processing point, not at RECEIVE. If D[k] is absent, it atomically appends e=(effect_id,k,p) to E and installs D[k]=(p,result,effect_id). If D[k] matches p, it leaves E,D unchanged and obtains the recorded result and effect ID. If the payload differs, it leaves E,D unchanged and obtains a mismatch rejection. The transition replaces xR with xC carrying that outcome; x remains absent from Q_R. ACK_ENQUEUE(x) requires xC, inserts alpha_x into Q_A, removes xC from V, and records T[x]=F. This enqueue/removal is one abstract transition, so it cannot emit two acknowledgments for one worker. ACK_DELIVER(alpha_x) removes that envelope from Q_A, appends its correlated response to L, and records delivery in J. It does not change T[x], E, or D. For the ordinary control, PROCESS always appends a fresh effect and leaves D empty, then creates xC in the same way.\\\",\\n      \\\"epistemic_status\\\": \\\"assumption\\\",\\n      \\\"basis_artifact_ids\\\": [\\n        \\\"4435b6ec-fefc-43a1-8706-a3a6794dbbe5\\\"\\n      ]\\n    },\\n    {\\n      \\\"title\\\": \\\"Crash boundary and request accounting\\\",\\n      \\\"argument\\\": \\\"CRASH clears every worker from V and sets the service down. For each xR it records T[x]=L0; for each xC it records T[x]=L1. It preserves E,D,Q_R,Q_A,L and prior terminal records. RESTART sets the service up with no workers; it reconstructs no consumed delivery. Thus a crash before RECEIVE leaves x queued, a crash after RECEIVE but before PROCESS loses x without an effect, a crash after PROCESS but before ACK_ENQUEUE loses only the volatile reply, and a crash after ACK_ENQUEUE leaves alpha_x pending in Q_A. A crash concurrent with atomic PROCESS is represented by either its before-state followed by CRASH or its complete after-state followed by CRASH; a partial E/D write is excluded by premise. The sent request IDs partition disjointly into Q_R, worker IDs in V, and terminal IDs in T. SEND introduces one ID, RECEIVE transfers it, PROCESS changes its worker phase, and enqueue/drop/crash transfers it to T. This proves complete request accounting inductively. Ack IDs similarly partition into Q_A and the delivered/dropped acknowledgment events in J. No automatic redelivery occurs after a pre-commit crash in this model; durable lease/redelivery semantics would be a different model.\\\",\\n      \\\"epistemic_status\\\": \\\"deduction\\\",\\n      \\\"basis_artifact_ids\\\": []\\n    },\\n    {\\n      \\\"title\\\": \\\"Durable invariant and ledger abbreviations\\\",\\n      \\\"argument\\\": \\\"For each key, invariant I is: either D[k] is absent and E contains no effect for k, or D[k]=(p,r,id) and E contains exactly one effect for k, namely (id,k,p), whose recorded result is r. Define Z=(E=empty,D=empty). Define P_x=(E={e_x},D[k]=(p,r_x,id_x)), with e_x=(id_x,k,p) created by delivery x. Define O_b=(E={e_b},D=empty) and O_ba=(E={e_b,e_a},D=empty) for the ordinary control. Z and every P_x satisfy I, including full payload and identifier correspondence, not just counts. O_b and O_ba fail I because ordinary mode intentionally has no D record; O_b still has at-most-one effect, whereas O_ba does not. In atomic mode, first PROCESS creates one matching pair, replay/rejection preserve it, and every other lifecycle transition leaves E,D unchanged. This proves I from empty initialization despite crashes and concurrent workers. It supplies safety only: loss of every ready worker can leave Z forever.\\\",\\n      \\\"epistemic_status\\\": \\\"deduction\\\",\\n      \\\"basis_artifact_ids\\\": [\\n        \\\"4435b6ec-fefc-43a1-8706-a3a6794dbbe5\\\"\\n      ]\\n    },\\n    {\\n      \\\"title\\\": \\\"T5: consumed request lost immediately before commit\\\",\\n      \\\"argument\\\": \\\"All requests below carry the same k,p. Each row is the state after the named event. Every durable state is Z or P_b, so I holds on every row.\\\\nEvent | Q_R | V | Q_A | T | E/D\\\\ninitial | - | - | - | - | Z\\\\nSEND a | a | - | - | - | Z\\\\nRECEIVE a | - | aR | - | - | Z\\\\nCRASH before PROCESS | - | - | - | a:L0 | Z\\\\nRESTART | - | - | - | a:L0 | Z\\\\ntimeout | - | - | - | a:L0 | Z\\\\nagent restore | - | - | - | a:L0 | Z\\\\nSEND retry b | b | - | - | a:L0 | Z\\\\nRECEIVE b | - | bR | - | a:L0 | Z\\\\nPROCESS b | - | bC | - | a:L0 | P_b\\\\nACK_ENQUEUE b | - | - | alpha_b | a:L0,b:F | P_b\\\\nACK_DELIVER alpha_b | - | - | - | a:L0,b:F | P_b\\\\nJ records alpha_b as delivered in the last row. Delivery a never reappears; only the new retry b creates the effect. Immediately before the crash, |Q_R|=0 but one unprocessed request still exists in V. Immediately afterward both queued and unprocessed-worker counts are zero. This resolves the earlier ambiguous q=0 notation.\\\",\\n      \\\"epistemic_status\\\": \\\"deduction\\\",\\n      \\\"basis_artifact_ids\\\": [\\n        \\\"4435b6ec-fefc-43a1-8706-a3a6794dbbe5\\\"\\n      ]\\n    },\\n    {\\n      \\\"title\\\": \\\"T5 boundary control: crash after commit, before acknowledgment enqueue\\\",\\n      \\\"argument\\\": \\\"This is the other crash boundary mentioned in the prior T5 description. I holds on every row, now using Z or P_a.\\\\nEvent | Q_R | V | Q_A | T | E/D\\\\ninitial | - | - | - | - | Z\\\\nSEND a | a | - | - | - | Z\\\\nRECEIVE a | - | aR | - | - | Z\\\\nPROCESS a | - | aC | - | - | P_a\\\\nCRASH before ACK_ENQUEUE | - | - | - | a:L1 | P_a\\\\nRESTART | - | - | - | a:L1 | P_a\\\\ntimeout | - | - | - | a:L1 | P_a\\\\nagent restore | - | - | - | a:L1 | P_a\\\\nSEND retry b | b | - | - | a:L1 | P_a\\\\nRECEIVE b | - | bR | - | a:L1 | P_a\\\\nPROCESS b, replay | - | bC | - | a:L1 | P_a\\\\nACK_ENQUEUE b | - | - | alpha_b | a:L1,b:F | P_a\\\\nACK_DELIVER alpha_b | - | - | - | a:L1,b:F | P_a\\\\nNo alpha_a was ever enqueued. The acknowledgment alpha_b contains the original r_a,id_a. J records alpha_b delivered. Actual completion survives a's lost reply; a's delivery itself is not reconstructed.\\\",\\n      \\\"epistemic_status\\\": \\\"deduction\\\",\\n      \\\"basis_artifact_ids\\\": [\\n        \\\"4435b6ec-fefc-43a1-8706-a3a6794dbbe5\\\"\\n      ]\\n    },\\n    {\\n      \\\"title\\\": \\\"T8: a delayed request remains live through lookup and retry\\\",\\n      \\\"argument\\\": \\\"Use the same event schedule for ordinary and atomic handlers. 'lookup' is a stipulated authoritative read of current effects, not a request added to this operation's Q; its query transport is outside this trace. It does not cancel or fence a. I_A holds on every row. I_O holds exactly on the Z rows and fails afterward by design.\\\\nEvent | Q_R | V | Q_A | T | ordinary E/D | atomic E/D\\\\ninitial | - | - | - | - | Z | Z\\\\nSEND a | a | - | - | - | Z | Z\\\\nDELAY a | a | - | - | - | Z | Z\\\\ntimeout | a | - | - | - | Z | Z\\\\nlookup: no effect | a | - | - | - | Z | Z\\\\nSEND retry b | a,b | - | - | - | Z | Z\\\\nRECEIVE b | a | bR | - | - | Z | Z\\\\nPROCESS b | a | bC | - | - | O_b | P_b\\\\nACK_ENQUEUE b | a | - | alpha_b | b:F | O_b | P_b\\\\nACK_DELIVER alpha_b | a | - | - | b:F | O_b | P_b\\\\nrelease delay a | a | - | - | b:F | O_b | P_b\\\\nRECEIVE a | - | aR | - | b:F | O_b | P_b\\\\nPROCESS a | - | aC | - | b:F | O_ba | P_b\\\\nACK_ENQUEUE a | - | - | alpha_a | a:F,b:F | O_ba | P_b\\\\nACK_DELIVER alpha_a | - | - | - | a:F,b:F | O_ba | P_b\\\\nJ records both acknowledgments delivered. Ordinary processing creates a second effect on PROCESS a. Atomic processing treats a as a replay and alpha_a returns r_b,id_b. The lookup was correct when made, yet left a live. Neither timeout nor delivery of alpha_b consumed a.\\\",\\n      \\\"epistemic_status\\\": \\\"deduction\\\",\\n      \\\"basis_artifact_ids\\\": [\\n        \\\"4435b6ec-fefc-43a1-8706-a3a6794dbbe5\\\"\\n      ]\\n    },\\n    {\\n      \\\"title\\\": \\\"T12: a received and processed first\\\",\\n      \\\"argument\\\": \\\"Two distinct deliveries have identical k,p. Both are dequeued before either PROCESS, allowing concurrent workers. Processing is serialized in order a,b. In particular test crashes before RECEIVE, after RECEIVE, after PROCESS, and after ACK_ENQUEUE against the stated loss semantics.\\\",\\n    \\\"Actual service atomicity, durability, retention, concurrency, collision prevention, payload rejection, and real-agent identity preservation remain unestablished; controlled recovery comparisons, independent judgments, uncertainty estimates, and cost reporting remain necessary.\\\",\\n    \\\"Previously recorded duties on lookup with fencing, escalation, compensation, safe termination, asymmetric harms, dependent workflows, and non-ledger outcome oracles are outside this refinement and remain unresolved.\\\",\\n    \\\"Obtain full historical sources before reconciliation: artifact 984e8fd3-f76b-46fb-b868-378c2f103425 is incomplete, finding df5067f1-d298-4203-a108-a2e7056af576 is omitted, and eleven prior historical obligations were not supplied in full.\\\"\\n  ],\\n  \\\"python_code\\\": null,\\n  \\\"sage_code\\\": null,\\n  \\\"prior_session_failure_attempt_ids\\\": [\\n    \\\"b49fd704-a709-41b9-a45b-62d1bf6df466\\\",\\n    \\\"f8466a1b-3066-49ee-9001-3e0c76699d04\\\"\\n  ],\\n  \\\"human_guidance_reviews\\\": [],\\n  \\\"computational_citations\\\": [],\\n  \\\"continuation_reviews\\\": []\\n}\"}\n\nevent: response.content_part.done\ndata: {\"type\":\"response.content_part.done\",\"content_index\":0,\"item_id\":\"msg_06057519e615f8d2016ae688b5878887d0ab1175c36ec3cd1c\",\"output_index\":2,\"part\":{\"type\":\"output_text\",\"annotations\":[],\"logprobs\":[],\"text\":\"{\\n  \\\"claim\\\": \\\"Under the explicit destructive-dequeue lifecycle defined here, RECEIVE removes a request delivery from Q and places it only in volatile V. A pre-commit service crash therefore loses that consumed delivery; it does not redeliver it. Requests still in Q survive the service crash. Conditional on serialized, crash-durable atomic effect/deduplication updates, the refined T5, T8, and both T12 orders preserve the durable E/D invariant. This closes the identified specification gap, not an implementation or experimental evidence gap.\\\",\\n  \\\"method\\\": \\\"Refine only the request lifecycle and manually evaluate the affected traces from empty durable state. The specification hypothesis is that explicitly separating dequeue, durable processing, and acknowledgment enqueue makes every request's fate determinate without changing the atomic E/D safety argument. The discriminating checks are delivery-ID conservation, exact pending and terminal request locations, and effect-record correspondence after every event. T8 includes an ordinary non-deduplicated control. These are manual deductions, not executed experiments. The relevant earlier timeout and interrupted review are operational limitations, not counterexamples; no unavailable runtime is requested. The supplied peer extracts 0310e2ff-4aa0-4c95-b1a8-795559e484b8 and faca8cd0-991f-46a4-91d4-288bb0cd53ea do not change this lifecycle choice: judge validity and actual service atomicity remain unverified, and no peer result is adopted as an independently established premise.\\\",\\n  \\\"reasoning_steps\\\": [\\n    {\\n      \\\"title\\\": \\\"State, identifiers, and table notation\\\",\\n      \\\"argument\\\": \\\"Retain S=(E,D,L,Q,V,J) from the supplied extract of artifact 4435b6ec-fefc-43a1-8706-a3a6794dbbe5. E is the durable effect multiset; D is the durable completed-record map; L is agent state; J is evaluator-only event history. Partition Q into request envelopes Q_R and acknowledgment envelopes Q_A. A request is (x,k,p), where delivery ID x is globally fresh, independently of stable operation key k. An acknowledgment has a fresh envelope ID alpha_x, correlation field x, and the processing outcome. Retries use a new delivery ID but the same k,p. Q is an independently maintained network-envelope pool: it survives service crashes but permits explicit DROP. It is not a durable broker with automatic redelivery. V contains a service up/down flag and volatile workers xR=(x,k,p,ready) or xC=(x,k,p,processed,outcome). Multiple workers are allowed. Tables display worker entries only; CRASH makes the service down and RESTART makes it up. '-' means empty. T is an evaluator-only terminal-request map derived from J, not additional recoverable service state: L0=lost before processing, L1=processed but reply lost before enqueue, F=handler finished with acknowledgment enqueued, X=explicitly dropped from Q_R. Each trace starts with empty E,D,Q,V,T and an up service.\\\",\\n      \\\"epistemic_status\\\": \\\"assumption\\\",\\n      \\\"basis_artifact_ids\\\": [\\n        \\\"4435b6ec-fefc-43a1-8706-a3a6794dbbe5\\\"\\n      ]\\n    },\\n    {\\n      \\\"title\\\": \\\"SEND, RECEIVE, delay, and drop\\\",\\n      \\\"argument\\\": \\\"SEND(x,k,p) adds exactly one fresh request envelope x to Q_R. RECEIVE(x) requires an up service and an eligible x in Q_R; it atomically removes x from Q_R and installs xR in V. RECEIVE changes neither E nor D and creates no acknowledgment. No copy or lease for x remains in Q. DELAY(x) makes no location change and merely withholds its RECEIVE until release. DROP(x) removes x from Q_R and records T[x]=X; dropping an acknowledgment instead removes its envelope from Q_A and records that acknowledgment's loss in J. A timeout does not remove an envelope or worker. Agent restore changes L only. There is no implicit duplicate delivery: an explicit retry is a new SEND with a fresh delivery ID.\\\",\\n      \\\"epistemic_status\\\": \\\"assumption\\\",\\n      \\\"basis_artifact_ids\\\": [\\n        \\\"4435b6ec-fefc-43a1-8706-a3a6794dbbe5\\\"\\n      ]\\n    },\\n    {\\n      \\\"title\\\": \\\"PROCESS is separate from acknowledgment enqueue\\\",\\n      \\\"argument\\\": \\\"PROCESS(x) requires xR and an up service. In atomic mode, it tests current D at the serialized processing point, not at RECEIVE. If D[k] is absent, it atomically appends e=(effect_id,k,p) to E and installs D[k]=(p,result,effect_id). If D[k] matches p, it leaves E,D unchanged and obtains the recorded result and effect ID. If the payload differs, it leaves E,D unchanged and obtains a mismatch rejection. The transition replaces xR with xC carrying that outcome; x remains absent from Q_R. ACK_ENQUEUE(x) requires xC, inserts alpha_x into Q_A, removes xC from V, and records T[x]=F. This enqueue/removal is one abstract transition, so it cannot emit two acknowledgments for one worker. ACK_DELIVER(alpha_x) removes that envelope from Q_A, appends its correlated response to L, and records delivery in J. It does not change T[x], E, or D. For the ordinary control, PROCESS always appends a fresh effect and leaves D empty, then creates xC in the same way.\\\",\\n      \\\"epistemic_status\\\": \\\"assumption\\\",\\n      \\\"basis_artifact_ids\\\": [\\n        \\\"4435b6ec-fefc-43a1-8706-a3a6794dbbe5\\\"\\n      ]\\n    },\\n    {\\n      \\\"title\\\": \\\"Crash boundary and request accounting\\\",\\n      \\\"argument\\\": \\\"CRASH clears every worker from V and sets the service down. For each xR it records T[x]=L0; for each xC it records T[x]=L1. It preserves E,D,Q_R,Q_A,L and prior terminal records. RESTART sets the service up with no workers; it reconstructs no consumed delivery. Thus a crash before RECEIVE leaves x queued, a crash after RECEIVE but before PROCESS loses x without an effect, a crash after PROCESS but before ACK_ENQUEUE loses only the volatile reply, and a crash after ACK_ENQUEUE leaves alpha_x pending in Q_A. A crash concurrent with atomic PROCESS is represented by either its before-state followed by CRASH or its complete after-state followed by CRASH; a partial E/D write is excluded by premise. The sent request IDs partition disjointly into Q_R, worker IDs in V, and terminal IDs in T. SEND introduces one ID, RECEIVE transfers it, PROCESS changes its worker phase, and enqueue/drop/crash transfers it to T. This proves complete request accounting inductively. Ack IDs similarly partition into Q_A and the delivered/dropped acknowledgment events in J. No automatic redelivery occurs after a pre-commit crash in this model; durable lease/redelivery semantics would be a different model.\\\",\\n      \\\"epistemic_status\\\": \\\"deduction\\\",\\n      \\\"basis_artifact_ids\\\": []\\n    },\\n    {\\n      \\\"title\\\": \\\"Durable invariant and ledger abbreviations\\\",\\n      \\\"argument\\\": \\\"For each key, invariant I is: either D[k] is absent and E contains no effect for k, or D[k]=(p,r,id) and E contains exactly one effect for k, namely (id,k,p), whose recorded result is r. Define Z=(E=empty,D=empty). Define P_x=(E={e_x},D[k]=(p,r_x,id_x)), with e_x=(id_x,k,p) created by delivery x. Define O_b=(E={e_b},D=empty) and O_ba=(E={e_b,e_a},D=empty) for the ordinary control. Z and every P_x satisfy I, including full payload and identifier correspondence, not just counts. O_b and O_ba fail I because ordinary mode intentionally has no D record; O_b still has at-most-one effect, whereas O_ba does not. In atomic mode, first PROCESS creates one matching pair, replay/rejection preserve it, and every other lifecycle transition leaves E,D unchanged. This proves I from empty initialization despite crashes and concurrent workers. It supplies safety only: loss of every ready worker can leave Z forever.\\\",\\n      \\\"epistemic_status\\\": \\\"deduction\\\",\\n      \\\"basis_artifact_ids\\\": [\\n        \\\"4435b6ec-fefc-43a1-8706-a3a6794dbbe5\\\"\\n      ]\\n    },\\n    {\\n      \\\"title\\\": \\\"T5: consumed request lost immediately before commit\\\",\\n      \\\"argument\\\": \\\"All requests below carry the same k,p. Each row is the state after the named event. Every durable state is Z or P_b, so I holds on every row.\\\\nEvent | Q_R | V | Q_A | T | E/D\\\\ninitial | - | - | - | - | Z\\\\nSEND a | a | - | - | - | Z\\\\nRECEIVE a | - | aR | - | - | Z\\\\nCRASH before PROCESS | - | - | - | a:L0 | Z\\\\nRESTART | - | - | - | a:L0 | Z\\\\ntimeout | - | - | - | a:L0 | Z\\\\nagent restore | - | - | - | a:L0 | Z\\\\nSEND retry b | b | - | - | a:L0 | Z\\\\nRECEIVE b | - | bR | - | a:L0 | Z\\\\nPROCESS b | - | bC | - | a:L0 | P_b\\\\nACK_ENQUEUE b | - | - | alpha_b | a:L0,b:F | P_b\\\\nACK_DELIVER alpha_b | - | - | - | a:L0,b:F | P_b\\\\nJ records alpha_b as delivered in the last row. Delivery a never reappears; only the new retry b creates the effect. Immediately before the crash, |Q_R|=0 but one unprocessed request still exists in V. Immediately afterward both queued and unprocessed-worker counts are zero. This resolves the earlier ambiguous q=0 notation.\\\",\\n      \\\"epistemic_status\\\": \\\"deduction\\\",\\n      \\\"basis_artifact_ids\\\": [\\n        \\\"4435b6ec-fefc-43a1-8706-a3a6794dbbe5\\\"\\n      ]\\n    },\\n    {\\n      \\\"title\\\": \\\"T5 boundary control: crash after commit, before acknowledgment enqueue\\\",\\n      \\\"argument\\\": \\\"This is the other crash boundary mentioned in the prior T5 description. Actual completion survives a's lost reply; a's delivery itself is not reconstructed.\\\",\\n      \\\"epistemic_status\\\": \\\"deduction\\\",\\n      \\\"basis_artifact_ids\\\": [\\n        \\\"4435b6ec-fefc-43a1-8706-a3a6794dbbe5\\\"\\n      ]\\n    },\\n    {\\n      \\\"title\\\": \\\"T8: a delayed request remains live through lookup and retry\\\",\\n      \\\"argument\\\": \\\"Use the same event schedule for ordinary and atomic handlers. I_O holds exactly on the Z rows and fails afterward by design.\\\\nEvent | Q_R | V | Q_A | T | ordinary E/D | atomic E/D\\\\ninitial | - | - | - | - | Z | Z\\\\nSEND a | a | - | - | - | Z | Z\\\\nDELAY a | a | - | - | - | Z | Z\\\\ntimeout | a | - | - | - | Z | Z\\\\nlookup: no effect | a | - | - | - | Z | Z\\\\nSEND retry b | a,b | - | - | - | Z | Z\\\\nRECEIVE b | a | bR | - | - | Z | Z\\\\nPROCESS b | a | bC | - | - | O_b | P_b\\\\nACK_ENQUEUE b | a | - | alpha_b | b:F | O_b | P_b\\\\nACK_DELIVER alpha_b | a | - | - | b:F | O_b | P_b\\\\nrelease delay a | a | - | - | b:F | O_b | P_b\\\\nRECEIVE a | - | aR | - | b:F | O_b | P_b\\\\nPROCESS a | - | aC | - | b:F | O_ba | P_b\\\\nACK_ENQUEUE a | - | - | alpha_a | a:F,b:F | O_ba | P_b\\\\nACK_DELIVER alpha_a | - | - | - | a:F,b:F | O_ba | P_b\\\\nJ records both acknowledgments delivered. Ordinary processing creates a second effect on PROCESS a. Atomic processing treats a as a replay and alpha_a returns r_b,id_b. The lookup was correct when made, yet left a live. In particular test crashes before RECEIVE, after RECEIVE, after PROCESS, and after ACK_ENQUEUE against the stated loss semantics.\\\",\\n    \\\"Actual service atomicity, durability, retention, concurrency, collision prevention, payload rejection, and real-agent identity preservation remain unestablished; controlled recovery comparisons, independent judgments, uncertainty estimates, and cost reporting remain necessary.\\\",\\n    \\\"Previously recorded duties on lookup with fencing, escalation, compensation, safe termination, asymmetric harms, dependent workflows, and non-ledger outcome oracles are outside this refinement and remain unresolved.\\\",\\n    \\\"Obtain full historical sources before reconciliation: artifact 984e8fd3-f76b-46fb-b868-378c2f103425 is incomplete, finding df5067f1-d298-4203-a108-a2e7056af576 is omitted, and eleven prior historical obligations were not supplied in full.\\\"\\n  ],\\n  \\\"python_code\\\": null,\\n  \\\"sage_code\\\": null,\\n  \\\"prior_session_failure_attempt_ids\\\": [\\n    \\\"b49fd704-a709-41b9-a45b-62d1bf6df466\\\",\\n    \\\"f8466a1b-3066-49ee-9001-3e0c76699d04\\\"\\n  ],\\n  \\\"human_guidance_reviews\\\": [],\\n  \\\"computational_citations\\\": [],\\n  \\\"continuation_reviews\\\": []\\n}\"},\"sequence_number\":4731}\n\nevent: response.output_item.done\ndata: {\"type\":\"response.output_item.done\",\"item\":{\"id\":\"msg_06057519e615f8d2016ae688b5878887d0ab1175c36ec3cd1c\",\"type\":\"message\",\"status\":\"completed\",\"content\":[{\"type\":\"output_text\",\"annotations\":[],\"logprobs\":[],\"text\":\"{\\n  \\\"claim\\\": \\\"Under the explicit destructive-dequeue lifecycle defined here, RECEIVE removes a request delivery from Q and places it only in volatile V. A pre-commit service crash therefore loses that consumed delivery; it does not redeliver it. Requests still in Q survive the service crash. Conditional on serialized, crash-durable atomic effect/deduplication updates, the refined T5, T8, and both T12 orders preserve the durable E/D invariant. This closes the identified specification gap, not an implementation or experimental evidence gap.\\\",\\n  \\\"method\\\": \\\"Refine only the request lifecycle and manually evaluate the affected traces from empty durable state. The specification hypothesis is that explicitly separating dequeue, durable processing, and acknowledgment enqueue makes every request's fate determinate without changing the atomic E/D safety argument. The discriminating checks are delivery-ID conservation, exact pending and terminal request locations, and effect-record correspondence after every event. T8 includes an ordinary non-deduplicated control. These are manual deductions, not executed experiments. The relevant earlier timeout and interrupted review are operational limitations, not counterexamples; no unavailable runtime is requested. The supplied peer extracts 0310e2ff-4aa0-4c95-b1a8-795559e484b8 and faca8cd0-991f-46a4-91d4-288bb0cd53ea do not change this lifecycle choice: judge validity and actual service atomicity remain unverified, and no peer result is adopted as an independently established premise.\\\",\\n  \\\"reasoning_steps\\\": [\\n    {\\n      \\\"title\\\": \\\"State, identifiers, and table notation\\\",\\n      \\\"argument\\\": \\\"Retain S=(E,D,L,Q,V,J) from the supplied extract of artifact 4435b6ec-fefc-43a1-8706-a3a6794dbbe5. E is the durable effect multiset; D is the durable completed-record map; L is agent state; J is evaluator-only event history. Partition Q into request envelopes Q_R and acknowledgment envelopes Q_A. A request is (x,k,p), where delivery ID x is globally fresh, independently of stable operation key k. An acknowledgment has a fresh envelope ID alpha_x, correlation field x, and the processing outcome. Retries use a new delivery ID but the same k,p. Q is an independently maintained network-envelope pool: it survives service crashes but permits explicit DROP. It is not a durable broker with automatic redelivery. V contains a service up/down flag and volatile workers xR=(x,k,p,ready) or xC=(x,k,p,processed,outcome). Multiple workers are allowed. Tables display worker entries only; CRASH makes the service down and RESTART makes it up. '-' means empty. T is an evaluator-only terminal-request map derived from J, not additional recoverable service state: L0=lost before processing, L1=processed but reply lost before enqueue, F=handler finished with acknowledgment enqueued, X=explicitly dropped from Q_R. Each trace starts with empty E,D,Q,V,T and an up service.\\\",\\n      \\\"epistemic_status\\\": \\\"assumption\\\",\\n      \\\"basis_artifact_ids\\\": [\\n        \\\"4435b6ec-fefc-43a1-8706-a3a6794dbbe5\\\"\\n      ]\\n    },\\n    {\\n      \\\"title\\\": \\\"SEND, RECEIVE, delay, and drop\\\",\\n      \\\"argument\\\": \\\"SEND(x,k,p) adds exactly one fresh request envelope x to Q_R. RECEIVE(x) requires an up service and an eligible x in Q_R; it atomically removes x from Q_R and installs xR in V. RECEIVE changes neither E nor D and creates no acknowledgment. No copy or lease for x remains in Q. DELAY(x) makes no location change and merely withholds its RECEIVE until release. DROP(x) removes x from Q_R and records T[x]=X; dropping an acknowledgment instead removes its envelope from Q_A and records that acknowledgment's loss in J. A timeout does not remove an envelope or worker. Agent restore changes L only. There is no implicit duplicate delivery: an explicit retry is a new SEND with a fresh delivery ID.\\\",\\n      \\\"epistemic_status\\\": \\\"assumption\\\",\\n      \\\"basis_artifact_ids\\\": [\\n        \\\"4435b6ec-fefc-43a1-8706-a3a6794dbbe5\\\"\\n      ]\\n    },\\n    {\\n      \\\"title\\\": \\\"PROCESS is separate from acknowledgment enqueue\\\",\\n      \\\"argument\\\": \\\"PROCESS(x) requires xR and an up service. In atomic mode, it tests current D at the serialized processing point, not at RECEIVE. If D[k] is absent, it atomically appends e=(effect_id,k,p) to E and installs D[k]=(p,result,effect_id). If D[k] matches p, it leaves E,D unchanged and obtains the recorded result and effect ID. If the payload differs, it leaves E,D unchanged and obtains a mismatch rejection. The transition replaces xR with xC carrying that outcome; x remains absent from Q_R. ACK_ENQUEUE(x) requires xC, inserts alpha_x into Q_A, removes xC from V, and records T[x]=F. This enqueue/removal is one abstract transition, so it cannot emit two acknowledgments for one worker. ACK_DELIVER(alpha_x) removes that envelope from Q_A, appends its correlated response to L, and records delivery in J. It does not change T[x], E, or D. For the ordinary control, PROCESS always appends a fresh effect and leaves D empty, then creates xC in the same way.\\\",\\n      \\\"epistemic_status\\\": \\\"assumption\\\",\\n      \\\"basis_artifact_ids\\\": [\\n        \\\"4435b6ec-fefc-43a1-8706-a3a6794dbbe5\\\"\\n      ]\\n    },\\n    {\\n      \\\"title\\\": \\\"Crash boundary and request accounting\\\",\\n      \\\"argument\\\": \\\"CRASH clears every worker from V and sets the service down. For each xR it records T[x]=L0; for each xC it records T[x]=L1. It preserves E,D,Q_R,Q_A,L and prior terminal records. RESTART sets the service up with no workers; it reconstructs no consumed delivery. Thus a crash before RECEIVE leaves x queued, a crash after RECEIVE but before PROCESS loses x without an effect, a crash after PROCESS but before ACK_ENQUEUE loses only the volatile reply, and a crash after ACK_ENQUEUE leaves alpha_x pending in Q_A. A crash concurrent with atomic PROCESS is represented by either its before-state followed by CRASH or its complete after-state followed by CRASH; a partial E/D write is excluded by premise. The sent request IDs partition disjointly into Q_R, worker IDs in V, and terminal IDs in T. SEND introduces one ID, RECEIVE transfers it, PROCESS changes its worker phase, and enqueue/drop/crash transfers it to T. This proves complete request accounting inductively. Ack IDs similarly partition into Q_A and the delivered/dropped acknowledgment events in J. No automatic redelivery occurs after a pre-commit crash in this model; durable lease/redelivery semantics would be a different model.\\\",\\n      \\\"epistemic_status\\\": \\\"deduction\\\",\\n      \\\"basis_artifact_ids\\\": []\\n    },\\n    {\\n      \\\"title\\\": \\\"Durable invariant and ledger abbreviations\\\",\\n      \\\"argument\\\": \\\"For each key, invariant I is: either D[k] is absent and E contains no effect for k, or D[k]=(p,r,id) and E contains exactly one effect for k, namely (id,k,p), whose recorded result is r. Define Z=(E=empty,D=empty). Define P_x=(E={e_x},D[k]=(p,r_x,id_x)), with e_x=(id_x,k,p) created by delivery x. Define O_b=(E={e_b},D=empty) and O_ba=(E={e_b,e_a},D=empty) for the ordinary control. Z and every P_x satisfy I, including full payload and identifier correspondence, not just counts. O_b and O_ba fail I because ordinary mode intentionally has no D record; O_b still has at-most-one effect, whereas O_ba does not. In atomic mode, first PROCESS creates one matching pair, replay/rejection preserve it, and every other lifecycle transition leaves E,D unchanged. This proves I from empty initialization despite crashes and concurrent workers. It supplies safety only: loss of every ready worker can leave Z forever.\\\",\\n      \\\"epistemic_status\\\": \\\"deduction\\\",\\n      \\\"basis_artifact_ids\\\": [\\n        \\\"4435b6ec-fefc-43a1-8706-a3a6794dbbe5\\\"\\n      ]\\n    },\\n    {\\n      \\\"title\\\": \\\"T5: consumed request lost immediately before commit\\\",\\n      \\\"argument\\\": \\\"All requests below carry the same k,p. Each row is the state after the named event. Every durable state is Z or P_b, so I holds on every row.\\\\nEvent | Q_R | V | Q_A | T | E/D\\\\ninitial | - | - | - | - | Z\\\\nSEND a | a | - | - | - | Z\\\\nRECEIVE a | - | aR | - | - | Z\\\\nCRASH before PROCESS | - | - | - | a:L0 | Z\\\\nRESTART | - | - | - | a:L0 | Z\\\\ntimeout | - | - | - | a:L0 | Z\\\\nagent restore | - | - | - | a:L0 | Z\\\\nSEND retry b | b | - | - | a:L0 | Z\\\\nRECEIVE b | - | bR | - | a:L0 | Z\\\\nPROCESS b | - | bC | - | a:L0 | P_b\\\\nACK_ENQUEUE b | - | - | alpha_b | a:L0,b:F | P_b\\\\nACK_DELIVER alpha_b | - | - | - | a:L0,b:F | P_b\\\\nJ records alpha_b as delivered in the last row. Delivery a never reappears; only the new retry b creates the effect. Immediately before the crash, |Q_R|=0 but one unprocessed request still exists in V. Immediately afterward both queued and unprocessed-worker counts are zero. This resolves the earlier ambiguous q=0 notation.\\\",\\n      \\\"epistemic_status\\\": \\\"deduction\\\",\\n      \\\"basis_artifact_ids\\\": [\\n        \\\"4435b6ec-fefc-43a1-8706-a3a6794dbbe5\\\"\\n      ]\\n    },\\n    {\\n      \\\"title\\\": \\\"T5 boundary control: crash after commit, before acknowledgment enqueue\\\",\\n      \\\"argument\\\": \\\"This is the other crash boundary mentioned in the prior T5 description. I holds on every row, now using Z or P_a.\\\\nEvent | Q_R | V | Q_A | T | E/D\\\\ninitial | - | - | - | - | Z\\\\nSEND a | a | - | - | - | Z\\\\nRECEIVE a | - | aR | - | - | Z\\\\nPROCESS a | - | aC | - | - | P_a\\\\nCRASH before ACK_ENQUEUE | - | - | - | a:L1 | P_a\\\\nRESTART | - | - | - | a:L1 | P_a\\\\ntimeout | - | - | - | a:L1 | P_a\\\\nagent restore | - | - | - | a:L1 | P_a\\\\nSEND retry b | b | - | - | a:L1 | P_a\\\\nRECEIVE b | - | bR | - | a:L1 | P_a\\\\nPROCESS b, replay | - | bC | - | a:L1 | P_a\\\\nACK_ENQUEUE b | - | - | alpha_b | a:L1,b:F | P_a\\\\nACK_DELIVER alpha_b | - | - | - | a:L1,b:F | P_a\\\\nNo alpha_a was ever enqueued. The acknowledgment alpha_b contains the original r_a,id_a. J records alpha_b delivered. Actual completion survives a's lost reply; a's delivery itself is not reconstructed.\\\",\\n      \\\"epistemic_status\\\": \\\"deduction\\\",\\n      \\\"basis_artifact_ids\\\": [\\n        \\\"4435b6ec-fefc-43a1-8706-a3a6794dbbe5\\\"\\n      ]\\n    },\\n    {\\n      \\\"title\\\": \\\"T8: a delayed request remains live through lookup and retry\\\",\\n      \\\"argument\\\": \\\"Use the same event schedule for ordinary and atomic handlers. 'lookup' is a stipulated authoritative read of current effects, not a request added to this operation's Q; its query transport is outside this trace. It does not cancel or fence a. I_A holds on every row. I_O holds exactly on the Z rows and fails afterward by design.\\\\nEvent | Q_R | V | Q_A | T | ordinary E/D | atomic E/D\\\\ninitial | - | - | - | - | Z | Z\\\\nSEND a | a | - | - | - | Z | Z\\\\nDELAY a | a | - | - | - | Z | Z\\\\ntimeout | a | - | - | - | Z | Z\\\\nlookup: no effect | a | - | - | - | Z | Z\\\\nSEND retry b | a,b | - | - | - | Z | Z\\\\nRECEIVE b | a | bR | - | - | Z | Z\\\\nPROCESS b | a | bC | - | - | O_b | P_b\\\\nACK_ENQUEUE b | a | - | alpha_b | b:F | O_b | P_b\\\\nACK_DELIVER alpha_b | a | - | - | b:F | O_b | P_b\\\\nrelease delay a | a | - | - | b:F | O_b | P_b\\\\nRECEIVE a | - | aR | - | b:F | O_b | P_b\\\\nPROCESS a | - | aC | - | b:F | O_ba | P_b\\\\nACK_ENQUEUE a | - | - | alpha_a | a:F,b:F | O_ba | P_b\\\\nACK_DELIVER alpha_a | - | - | - | a:F,b:F | O_ba | P_b\\\\nJ records both acknowledgments delivered. Ordinary processing creates a second effect on PROCESS a. Atomic processing treats a as a replay and alpha_a returns r_b,id_b. The lookup was correct when made, yet left a live. Neither timeout nor delivery of alpha_b consumed a.\\\",\\n      \\\"epistemic_status\\\": \\\"deduction\\\",\\n      \\\"basis_artifact_ids\\\": [\\n        \\\"4435b6ec-fefc-43a1-8706-a3a6794dbbe5\\\"\\n      ]\\n    },\\n    {\\n      \\\"title\\\": \\\"T12: a received and processed first\\\",\\n      \\\"argument\\\": \\\"Two distinct deliveries have identical k,p. Both are dequeued before either PROCESS, allowing concurrent workers. Processing is serialized in order a,b. I holds on every row.\\\\nEvent | Q_R | V | Q_A | T | E/D\\\\ninitial | - | - | - | - | Z\\\\nSEND a | a | - | - | - | Z\\\\nSEND b | a,b | - | - | - | Z\\\\nRECEIVE a | b | aR | - | - | Z\\\\nRECEIVE b | - | aR,bR | - | - | Z\\\\nPROCESS a | - | aC,bR | - | - | P_a\\\\nPROCESS b, replay | - | aC,bC | - | - | P_a\\\\nACK_ENQUEUE a | - | bC | alpha_a | a:F | P_a\\\\nACK_ENQUEUE b | - | - | alpha_a,alpha_b | a:F,b:F | P_a\\\\nACK_DELIVER alpha_a | - | - | alpha_b | a:F,b:F | P_a\\\\nACK_DELIVER alpha_b | - | - | - | a:F,b:F | P_a\\\\nBoth acknowledgments carry r_a,id_a; J records both delivered. Dequeuing b while D is absent does not reserve permission to create an effect: its PROCESS tests D after a's serialized commit.\\\",\\n      \\\"epistemic_status\\\": \\\"deduction\\\",\\n      \\\"basis_artifact_ids\\\": [\\n        \\\"4435b6ec-fefc-43a1-8706-a3a6794dbbe5\\\"\\n      ]\\n    },\\n    {\\n      \\\"title\\\": \\\"T12: b received and processed first\\\",\\n      \\\"argument\\\": \\\"Reverse delivery and processing order to b,a, retaining the same two sends. I holds on every row.\\\\nEvent | Q_R | V | Q_A | T | E/D\\\\ninitial | - | - | - | - | Z\\\\nSEND a | a | - | - | - | Z\\\\nSEND b | a,b | - | - | - | Z\\\\nRECEIVE b | a | bR | - | - | Z\\\\nRECEIVE a | - | aR,bR | - | - | Z\\\\nPROCESS b | - | aR,bC | - | - | P_b\\\\nPROCESS a, replay | - | aC,bC | - | - | P_b\\\\nACK_ENQUEUE b | - | aC | alpha_b | b:F | P_b\\\\nACK_ENQUEUE a | - | - | alpha_a,alpha_b | a:F,b:F | P_b\\\\nACK_DELIVER alpha_b | - | - | alpha_a | a:F,b:F | P_b\\\\nACK_DELIVER alpha_a | - | - | - | a:F,b:F | P_b\\\\nBoth acknowledgments carry r_b,id_b; J records both delivered. Receive order need not equal processing order: after both RECEIVE events, the ready-worker state is identical in these tables. Choosing either PROCESS first therefore also covers the crossed receive/processing orders. The unique effect ID may differ across alternative executions; within each execution both replies identify its single effect.\\\",\\n      \\\"epistemic_status\\\": \\\"deduction\\\",\\n      \\\"basis_artifact_ids\\\": [\\n        \\\"4435b6ec-fefc-43a1-8706-a3a6794dbbe5\\\"\\n      ]\\n    },\\n    {\\n      \\\"title\\\": \\\"Scope and status of the refinement\\\",\\n      \\\"argument\\\": \\\"The explicit RECEIVE and crash rules address the local lifecycle gap recorded in obligations 041a5bf1f13d8ecadcaa67e9f85d9c6defcf7c0292878c28561d3282ac397e9f, f05f8609355469e012f0af211587c3b08e72540487597f0d788953675e46e7a8, and 99bdafb61848d9f5dafb4c29a1e310392c4262e9a6a896d6054f449a64d45cd9 at the specification level only. The loss rule is an explicit model choice consistent with the earlier T5 expectation, not a claim about deployed queues. A durable redelivery model would need retained ownership/lease state and different T5 accounting. These manual tables supply reproducible expected states and distinguish effect safety from transport liveness; they do not establish model-to-system correspondence, observation isolation, or engineering benefit. Standard state-machine reasoning is used; material novelty and empirical generality are not assessed. Only the supplied extracts were examined. The incomplete historical finding, one omitted finding, and eleven omitted historical obligations remain unreconciled.\\\",\\n      \\\"epistemic_status\\\": \\\"deduction\\\",\\n      \\\"basis_artifact_ids\\\": [\\n        \\\"4435b6ec-fefc-43a1-8706-a3a6794dbbe5\\\",\\n        \\\"984e8fd3-f76b-46fb-b868-378c2f103425\\\"\\n      ]\\n    }\\n  ],\\n  \\\"claim_is_conditional\\\": true,\\n  \\\"assumptions\\\": [\\n    \\\"The modeled operation is ledger-backed, and all its effects occur through the defined PROCESS transition; E and D initially are empty.\\\",\\n    \\\"RECEIVE is destructive dequeue into volatile execution state, with no retained broker lease or automatic redelivery. The independent envelope pool Q survives service crashes; explicit network drops remain possible.\\\",\\n    \\\"Atomic mode serializes the current-D test, effect creation, and completed-record write in one crash-durable transition. Records are retained, operation keys do not collide, and all retries in these traces preserve the same full payload and key.\\\",\\n    \\\"PROCESS and ACK_ENQUEUE are distinct abstract transitions; ACK_ENQUEUE atomically transfers a processed worker into one pending acknowledgment. Crashes preserve durable E/D and Q but erase all workers.\\\",\\n    \\\"The manual traces use exactly the displayed schedules. They establish no fairness or eventual-processing property for arbitrary executions.\\\"\\n  ],\\n  \\\"evidence_status\\\": \\\"Specification refinement with an explicit accounting argument and manually derived finite trace tables. No computation, implementation, service audit, agent trial, literature inspection, or external verification occurred. The pre-commit lifecycle ambiguity is resolved within the chosen model; empirical and historical obligations remain open.\\\",\\n  \\\"open_obligations\\\": [\\n    \\\"When execution becomes available, implement and independently audit the refined transitions, replay T0–T12 with per-event delivery accounting and E/D checks, and audit the observation projection and effect oracle. In particular test crashes before RECEIVE, after RECEIVE, after PROCESS, and after ACK_ENQUEUE against the stated loss semantics.\\\",\\n    \\\"Actual service atomicity, durability, retention, concurrency, collision prevention, payload rejection, and real-agent identity preservation remain unestablished; controlled recovery comparisons, independent judgments, uncertainty estimates, and cost reporting remain necessary.\\\",\\n    \\\"Previously recorded duties on lookup with fencing, escalation, compensation, safe termination, asymmetric harms, dependent workflows, and non-ledger outcome oracles are outside this refinement and remain unresolved.\\\",\\n    \\\"Obtain full historical sources before reconciliation: artifact 984e8fd3-f76b-46fb-b868-378c2f103425 is incomplete, finding df5067f1-d298-4203-a108-a2e7056af576 is omitted, and eleven prior historical obligations were not supplied in full.\\\"\\n  ],\\n  \\\"python_code\\\": null,\\n  \\\"sage_code\\\": null,\\n  \\\"prior_session_failure_attempt_ids\\\": [\\n    \\\"b49fd704-a709-41b9-a45b-62d1bf6df466\\\",\\n    \\\"f8466a1b-3066-49ee-9001-3e0c76699d04\\\"\\n  ],\\n  \\\"human_guidance_reviews\\\": [],\\n  \\\"computational_citations\\\": [],\\n  \\\"continuation_reviews\\\": []\\n}\"}],\"phase\":\"final_answer\",\"role\":\"assistant\"},\"output_index\":2,\"sequence_number\":4732}\n\nevent: response.completed\ndata: {\"type\":\"response.completed\",\"response\":{\"id\":\"resp_06057519e615f8d2016ae68893e30887d09481371306cb4f0d\",\"object\":\"response\",\"created_at\":1793493139,\"status\":\"completed\",\"access_programs\":{\"cyber\":\"standard\"},\"background\":false,\"completed_at\":1793493314,\"error\":null,\"frequency_penalty\":0.0,\"incomplete_details\":null,\"instructions\":\"You are an investigator in a bounded research session.         "content": "{\"problem\": \"Autonomous AI agents are increasingly expected to complete complex tasks involving planning, reasoning, external tools, persistent state, and interaction with changing environments. Demonstrations and benchmark results show that agents can perform many such tasks, but provide limited evidence that they remain dependable across repeated executions, unfamiliar conditions, long-running workflows, and settings where mistakes have significant consequences. This project asks how autonomous and semi-autonomous agents can be evaluated and engineered to deliver reliable, correct, recoverable, and reproducible results across extended, multi-step tasks.\\n\\nAgent reliability is a system-level property. Probabilistic decisions, dynamically constructed plans, incomplete observations, tool interfaces, memory, orchestration, and external state all affect whether the intended outcome is actually achieved. Small errors can propagate through later actions and yield plausible but incorrect results. An agent may claim completion without satisfying the task, recover from one failure while introducing another, or behave differently across otherwise comparable runs. Reliability therefore cannot be inferred from fluent explanations, a single successful trajectory, agreement among similar models, or benchmark scores alone.\\n\\nInvestigate three connected questions. First, how should reliability be defined and measured so evaluation reflects actual correctness, robustness, consistency, recoverability, tool-use quality, and cost rather than superficial completion? Second, what are the principal sources of failure, how do errors propagate through multi-step execution, and which signals and interventions can detect, contain, or recover from failures without creating additional risks? Third, which engineering mechanisms demonstrably improve outcomes, and how can their effects be established through controlled experiments rather than architectural intuition or anecdotal success? The strategies approach these questions from complementary measurement, failure-analysis, and intervention perspectives; none presumes a preferred architecture.\\n\\nUse available research literature, software-reliability principles, empirical evaluation methods, and documented agent-system designs. Examine the relationship between model capability and end-to-end system reliability, including tool interfaces, state management, verification, orchestration, uncertainty handling, changing environments, recovery, and execution budgets. Assess benchmark sensitivity to task selection, evaluator bias, contamination, and weak completion oracles. Consider stochastic behavior, repeated trials, long dependency chains, held-out tasks, fault injection, independent correctness judgments, and uncertainty in estimated success rates. Where comparisons are proposed, make assumptions and controls explicit, including model and prompt versions, task difficulty, environment, tool access, compute, latency, and monetary budgets.\\n\\nEvaluate competing approaches on the strength and limits of their evidence. Distinguish measured results from formal or theoretical arguments, proposed mechanisms, and unsupported claims; do not present planned experiments as completed or infer causal benefit from correlation. Account for correlated errors among agents or critics that share models and training data, and for the difficulty of constructing an independent oracle for open-ended tasks. Analyze tradeoffs among reliability, flexibility, recovery overhead, latency, and computational expense, including cases where a safeguard shifts rather than removes risk.\\n\\nThe intended outcome is an evidence-grounded account of what reliability claims current evaluations can support, a practical and reproducible evaluation framework, a causal taxonomy of important failure and recovery modes, and architectural principles whose limits are explicit. Identify unresolved questions and specify discriminating experiments needed to validate competing claims. Examine incorrect reasoning and plans, tool misuse, incomplete observations, stale or compressed context, instruction misunderstandings, environmental changes, and accumulated state errors. Trace concrete failure chains from initiating fault through subsequent actions to user-visible consequences; distinguish model limitations from architecture, orchestration, memory, interface, and environment failures. Investigate detection of silent errors, calibrated uncertainty versus actual failure, retry and replanning policies, escalation, and safe termination. Analyze checkpointing, state reconstruction, independent verification, rollback, idempotency, and human intervention as recovery mechanisms. For each mechanism, specify assumptions, failure modes, and measurable recovery criteria; compare recovery against restarting and continuing without intervention. DROP permanently removes an envelope before processing; DELAY leaves it eligible for later processing. A service crash discards V but preserves E and D; it does not implicitly cancel network envelopes. Agent restore changes L to its checkpoint but cannot change E,D, or Q. The agent observes only its configured projection: L, delivered tool messages, and a controlled logical clock. It cannot inspect E,D,Q,J or hidden service metadata in the local-only arm. This restriction must be enforced and audited in an implementation; it is not an assertion about ordinary deployed tools.\", \"epistemic_status\": \"assumption\", \"basis_artifact_ids\": [], \"review\": {\"disposition\": \"accepted\", \"rationale\": \"The stated premises consistently distinguish permanent drop from delay, preserve external durable state across local restoration, and restrict agent observations. If D[k] is absent, it simultaneously appends one effect e=(id,k,p) to E and installs D[k]=(p,result,id). If D[k] contains the same full payload, it returns the recorded result without changing E or D. If the payload differs, it rejects without an effect. A crash during the atomic transition exposes either its entire before-state or its entire after-state. Starting with E=D=empty, the invariant is: for each key, either D is absent and no effect exists, or D identifies exactly one matching effect and no other effect exists for that key. Induction proves it: an absent-key transition creates precisely the matching pair; replay and rejection preserve it; SEND, DROP, DELAY, acknowledgment handling, and crashes do not alter the pair. Atomic serialization covers simultaneous requests, so both cannot observe an absent key at their commit points. Thus any finite sequence, including delayed duplicate deliveries, preserves at-most-one effect.\", \"epistemic_status\": \"deduction\", \"basis_artifact_ids\": [], \"review\": {\"disposition\": \"accepted\", \"rationale\": \"Starting from empty E and D, each permitted durable-state transition preserves the claimed correspondence. This establishes per-key safety only under the stated atomicity and retention premises.\", \"objection\": \"\", \"basis_artifact_ids\": []}, \"research_artifact_id\": \"4435b6ec-fefc-43a1-8706-a3a6794dbbe5\"}, {\"number\": 4, \"title\": \"Separate safety, eventual effect, and verified completion\", \"argument\": \"The invariant does not imply that an effect ever occurs: all requests might be dropped, or execution might stop before processing. If at least one matching request completes PROCESS, its absent-key branch creates one effect or its replay branch witnesses an existing matching effect. Combining this existence argument with at-most-one gives exactly one effect. An acknowledgment need not reach the agent, so actual correctness does not imply verified completion. Conversely, a finite-time observation of one effect need not establish stable success when a non-deduplicated request remains pending. Skipping leaves effect counts 0 and 1 respectively; issuing one successfully processed retry leaves counts 1 and 2. Crash immediately after commit but before acknowledgment instead leaves (1,1,0); retry preserves it. The required checks are the full payload, effect identifier, record-effect correspondence, and invariant after every transition, not merely the final count. They are model definitions, not established deployment properties.\", \"objection\": \"\", \"basis_artifact_ids\": []}, \"research_artifact_id\": \"4435b6ec-fefc-43a1-8706-a3a6794dbbe5\"}, {\"number\": 3, \"title\": \"Define atomic processing and prove its safety invariant\", \"argument\": \"An atomic PROCESS(k,p) transition behaves as follows. If D[k] is absent, it simultaneously appends one effect e=(id,k,p) to E and installs D[k]=(p,result,id). If D[k] contains the same full payload, it returns the recorded result without changing E or D. If the payload differs, it rejects without an effect. A crash during the atomic transition exposes either its entire before-state or its entire after-state. Starting with E=D=empty, the invariant is: for each key, either D is absent and no effect exists, or D identifies exactly one matching effect and no other effect exists for that key. Induction proves it: an absent-key transition creates precisely the matching pair; replay and rejection preserve it; SEND, DROP, DELAY, acknowledgment handling, and crashes do not alter the pair. Atomic serialization covers simultaneous requests, so both cannot observe an absent key at their commit points. Thus any finite sequence, including delayed duplicate deliveries, preserves at-most-one effect.\", \"epistemic_status\": \"deduction\", \"basis_artifact_ids\": [], \"review\": {\"disposition\": \"accepted\", \"rationale\": \"Starting from empty E and D, each permitted durable-state transition preserves the claimed correspondence. Serialization prevents two absent-key commits, and all other listed transitions leave the pair unchanged. This establishes per-key safety only under the stated atomicity and retention premises.\", \"objection\": \"\", \"basis_artifact_ids\": []}, \"research_artifact_id\": \"4435b6ec-fefc-43a1-8706-a3a6794dbbe5\"}, {\"number\": 4, \"title\": \"Separate safety, eventual effect, and verified completion\", \"argument\": \"The invariant does not imply that an effect ever occurs: all requests might be dropped, or execution might stop before processing. If at least one matching request completes PROCESS, its absent-key branch creates one effect or its replay branch witnesses an existing matching effect. Combining this existence argument with at-most-one gives exactly one effect. An acknowledgment need not reach the agent, so actual correctness does not imply verified completion. Conversely, a finite-time observation of one effect need not establish stable success when a non-deduplicated request remains pending. Final audits must drain all accepted requests under a declared schedule or establish that they have been irrevocably fenced; a timeout alone is not such a fence.\", \"epistemic_status\": \"deduction\", \"basis_artifact_ids\": [], \"review\": {\"disposition\": \"accepted\", \"rationale\": \"With the stable matching key and payload, a completed PROCESS either creates the effect or observes its existing matching record. Combining existence with the invariant gives exactly one. Lost acknowledgments and live ordinary requests correctly separate actual correctness, agent knowledge, and stable finality.\", \"objection\": \"\", \"basis_artifact_ids\": []}, \"research_artifact_id\": \"4435b6ec-fefc-43a1-8706-a3a6794dbbe5\"}, {\"number\": 5, \"title\": \"Manually derive the ordinary-operation ambiguity controls\", \"argument\": \"Write a summary state as (N,d,q), where N counts intended-key effects, d=1 means a completed D entry exists, and q counts outstanding requests; omitted acknowledgments are stated separately. In ordinary mode, processing always appends an effect and leaves D empty. T0, no fault: SEND; PROCESS; deliver acknowledgment gives (1,0,0) and visible success. T1, pre-commit loss: SEND; DROP; timeout gives (0,0,0). T2, post-commit acknowledgment loss: SEND; PROCESS; DROP acknowledgment; timeout gives (1,0,0). Restore the same intent checkpoint and expose the same logical-time timeout transcript in T1 and T2. Their agent projections must then be byte-for-byte equal despite different E. Skipping leaves effect counts 0 and 1 respectively; issuing one successfully processed retry leaves counts 1 and 2. This reproduces the relevant ambiguity without assuming an implemented harness already hides every side channel.\", \"epistemic_status\": \"deduction\", \"basis_artifact_ids\": [], \"review\": {\"disposition\": \"accepted\", \"rationale\": \"The completed ordinary-operation traces yield effect counts zero and one at the timeout, and one and two after a successful retry. T5, crash immediately before the atomic commit leaves (0,0,0) after the consumed request is lost; retry creates (1,1,0). Crash immediately after commit but before acknowledgment instead leaves (1,1,0); retry preserves it. The required checks are the full payload, effect identifier, record-effect correspondence, and invariant after every transition, not merely the final count. These are consequences of the atomic model, not evidence that a specific service implements it.\", \"epistemic_status\": \"deduction\", \"basis_artifact_ids\": [], \"review\": {\"disposition\": \"unresolved\", \"rationale\": \"T3/T4 and the durable-state outcomes around atomic commitment follow from the handler. T7, record first: write a completed record containing a reserved effect identifier, giving (0,1,0); crash before creating that effect; retry treats D as completed and returns success without an effect, leaving (0,1,0). T6 violates at-most-one; T7 violates completed-record soundness and exactly-one. Both failures occur with stable key and payload. These traces refute sufficiency of this naive two-write handler, not all non-atomic implementations: a pending-state protocol with durable recovery, fencing, or downstream deduplication requires separate analysis.\", \"epistemic_status\": \"deduction\", \"basis_artifact_ids\": [], \"review\": {\"disposition\": \"accepted\", \"rationale\": \"For these explicitly naive handlers, effect-first leaves a durable effect without a record, enabling a second effect; record-first leaves a completed record without its effect, causing a false replay success. Treat this as a specification, not an [truncated; inspect the original saved artifact]\"}, \"session_id\": \"a1a9ab51-f8d1-4b60-ba10-baad7585a34f\", \"session_number\": 1, \"strategy_id\": \"843ffb99-1d7b-476b-973f-845d79d4b6e3\", \"strategy_title\": \"Develop a rigorous framework for measuring AI agent reliability\", \"extract_truncated_fields\": [\"evidence_status\", \"next_question\", \"skeptic_output.next_question\", \"reasoning_steps\", \"assumptions\", \"open_obligations\"], \"reasoning_steps\": [{\"number\": 1, \"title\": \"Define the operation, objective, and observation boundary\", \"epistemic_status\": \"assumption\", \"basis_artifact_ids\": [], \"argument\": \"Consider an agent instructed to cause exactly one irreversible external effect, such as appending one shipment order. Each accepted ordinary request creates one effect; there is no built-in deduplication. Let N be the external effect count for this task. Correctness is N=1, not merely receiving a plausible response. The agent records the same local intent before sending the request. At a timeout, its accessible checkpoint, messages, and observations do not reveal whether that request committed. Assume the only terminal recovery choices are skip or one retry; the retry, if chosen, commits exactly one additional effect. This intentionally restricted model isolates ambiguous-commit recovery rather than arbitrary tool or model errors.\", \"review\": {\"disposition\": \"accepted\", \"rationale\": \"The operation, success predicate N=1, observation boundary, and restricted terminal actions define a coherent model. They are accepted as premises only because the claim is explicitly conditional on them.\", \"objection\": \"\"}}, {\"number\": 2, \"title\": \"Construct two indistinguishable fault histories\", \"epistemic_status\": \"deduction\", \"basis_artifact_ids\": [], \"argument\": \"In history H0, the initial request is lost before commitment, leaving N=0. In history H1, the request commits, leaving N=1, but its acknowledgment is lost. Both histories end at the same timeout with the same local intent record and no acknowledgment. By assumption, no authoritative status lookup or other distinguishing observation is available before the decision. Therefore a policy using only that local information must use the same retry probability q in both histories. Random internal reasoning or replanning cannot distinguish two histories when its inputs and randomization distribution are identical.\", \"review\": {\"disposition\": \"accepted\", \"rationale\": \"Given identical accessible histories and identical policy-randomization distributions, a local-information policy must assign the same probability to retrying. H0 and H1 differ only in evaluator-visible external effect count.\", \"objection\": \"\"}}, {\"number\": 3, \"title\": \"Derive the sharp worst-case error bound\", \"epistemic_status\": \"deduction\", \"basis_artifact_ids\": [], \"argument\": \"In H0, skipping leaves N=0 and retrying yields N=1, so the error probability is e0=1-q. In H1, skipping preserves N=1 and retrying yields N=2, so e1=q. Consequently e0+e1=1 and max(e0,e1)>=1/2. Equality is attained by q=1/2, making the bound sharp within this model. The deterministic edge cases q=0 and q=1 each fail with probability one in one history. This is a worst-case bound over two possible histories, not an assertion that either history occurs equally often in deployment.\", \"review\": {\"disposition\": \"accepted\", \"rationale\": \"Under the stipulated successful retry, H0 fails exactly when the policy skips, whereas H1 fails exactly when it retries. Thus e0=1-q, e1=q, their sum is one, and their maximum is at least one half; q=1/2 attains equality.\", \"objection\": \"\"}}, {\"number\": 4, \"title\": \"Separate worst-case reliability from deployment-average reliability\", \"epistemic_status\": \"deduction\", \"basis_artifact_ids\": [], \"argument\": \"If H1 has known conditional probability p among ambiguous timeouts, expected error is (1-p)(1-q)+pq. This affine function is minimized at q=1 when p<1/2, at q=0 when p>1/2, and by any q when p=1/2. The minimum is min(p,1-p). Thus an excellent average result can coexist with certain failure in the rarer history. The expression applies only within the ambiguous-timeout population and with equal weighting of missing and duplicate effects; it is not an overall task failure rate or an appropriate loss function when duplicate effects are more harmful.\", \"review\": {\"disposition\": \"accepted\", \"rationale\": \"Weighting the two conditional errors by 1-p and p gives 1-p+(2p-1)q. Its slope yields the stated optimal endpoint policies and minimum min(p,1-p). The equal-loss and ambiguous-timeout conditioning restrictions are explicitly preserved.\", \"objection\": \"\"}}], \"obligation_reviews\": [{\"obligation_id\": reliability\", \"approach\": \"\", \"enabled\": null, \"eligibility\": \"eligible\", \"removed_at\": null}], \"investigator_step_id\": \"a0201cba-781e-418a-9bdd-116e4d770c96\", \"investigator_output\": {\"claim\": \"Under the explicit destructive-dequeue lifecycle defined here, RECEIVE removes a request delivery from Q and places it only in volatile V. A pre-commit service crash therefore loses that consumed delivery; it does not redeliver it. Requests still in Q survive the service crash. Conditional on serialized, crash-durable atomic effect/deduplication updates, the refined T5, T8, and both T12 orders preserve the durable E/D invariant. This closes the identified specification gap, not an implementation or experimental evidence gap.\", \"method\": \"Refine only the request lifecycle and manually evaluate the affected traces from empty durable state. The specification hypothesis is that explicitly separating dequeue, durable processing, and acknowledgment enqueue makes every request's fate determinate without changing the atomic E/D safety argument. The discriminating checks are delivery-ID conservation, exact pending and terminal request locations, and effect-record correspondence after every event. T8 includes an ordinary non-deduplicated control. These are manual deductions, not executed experiments. The relevant earlier timeout and interrupted review are operational limitations, not counterexamples; no unavailable runtime is requested. The supplied peer extracts 0310e2ff-4aa0-4c95-b1a8-795559e484b8 and faca8cd0-991f-46a4-91d4-288bb0cd53ea do not change this lifecycle choice: judge validity and actual service atomicity remain unverified, and no peer result is adopted as an independently established premise.\", \"reasoning_steps\": [{\"title\": \"State, identifiers, and table notation\", \"argument\": \"Retain S=(E,D,L,Q,V,J) from the supplied extract of artifact 4435b6ec-fefc-43a1-8706-a3a6794dbbe5. E is the durable effect multiset; D is the durable completed-record map; L is agent state; J is evaluator-only event history. Partition Q into request envelopes Q_R and acknowledgment envelopes Q_A. A request is (x,k,p), where delivery ID x is globally fresh, independently of stable operation key k. An acknowledgment has a fresh envelope ID alpha_x, correlation field x, and the processing outcome. Retries use a new delivery ID but the same k,p. Q is an independently maintained network-envelope pool: it survives service crashes but permits explicit DROP. It is not a durable broker with automatic redelivery. V contains a service up/down flag and volatile workers xR=(x,k,p,ready) or xC=(x,k,p,processed,outcome). Multiple workers are allowed. Tables display worker entries only; CRASH makes the service down and RESTART makes it up. '-' means empty. T is an evaluator-only terminal-request map derived from J, not additional recoverable service state: L0=lost before processing, L1=processed but reply lost before enqueue, F=handler finished with acknowledgment enqueued, X=explicitly dropped from Q_R. Each trace starts with empty E,D,Q,V,T and an up service.\", \"epistemic_status\": \"assumption\", \"basis_artifact_ids\": [\"4435b6ec-fefc-43a1-8706-a3a6794dbbe5\"]}, {\"title\": \"SEND, RECEIVE, delay, and drop\", \"argument\": \"SEND(x,k,p) adds exactly one fresh request envelope x to Q_R. RECEIVE(x) requires an up service and an eligible x in Q_R; it atomically removes x from Q_R and installs xR in V. RECEIVE changes neither E nor D and creates no acknowledgment. No copy or lease for x remains in Q. DELAY(x) makes no location change and merely withholds its RECEIVE until release. DROP(x) removes x from Q_R and records T[x]=X; dropping an acknowledgment instead removes its envelope from Q_A and records that acknowledgment's loss in J. A timeout does not remove an envelope or worker. Agent restore changes L only. There is no implicit duplicate delivery: an explicit retry is a new SEND with a fresh delivery ID.\", \"epistemic_status\": \"assumption\", \"basis_artifact_ids\": [\"4435b6ec-fefc-43a1-8706-a3a6794dbbe5\"]}, {\"title\": \"PROCESS is separate from acknowledgment enqueue\", \"argument\": \"PROCESS(x) requires xR and an up service. In atomic mode, it tests current D at the serialized processing point, not at RECEIVE. If D[k] is absent, it atomically appends e=(effect_id,k,p) to E and installs D[k]=(p,result,effect_id). If D[k] matches p, it leaves E,D unchanged and obtains the recorded result and effect ID. If the payload differs, it leaves E,D unchanged and obtains a mismatch rejection. The transition replaces xR with xC carrying that outcome; x remains absent from Q_R. ACK_ENQUEUE(x) requires xC, inserts alpha_x into Q_A, removes xC from V, and records T[x]=F. This enqueue/removal is one abstract transition, so it cannot emit two acknowledgments for one worker. ACK_DELIVER(alpha_x) removes that envelope from Q_A, appends its correlated response to L, and records delivery in J. It does not change T[x], E, or D. For the ordinary control, PROCESS always appends a fresh effect and leaves D empty, then creates xC in the same way.\", \"epistemic_status\": \"assumption\", \"basis_artifact_ids\": [\"4435b6ec-fefc-43a1-8706-a3a6794dbbe5\"]}, {\"title\": \"Crash boundary and request accounting\", \"argument\": \"CRASH clears every worker from V and sets the service down. For each xR it records T[x]=L0; for each xC it records T[x]=L1. It preserves E,D,Q_R,Q_A,L and prior terminal records. RESTART sets the service up with no workers; it reconstructs no consumed delivery. Thus a crash before RECEIVE leaves x queued, a crash after RECEIVE but before PROCESS loses x without an effect, a crash after PROCESS but before ACK_ENQUEUE loses only the volatile reply, and a crash after ACK_ENQUEUE leaves alpha_x pending in Q_A. A crash concurrent with atomic PROCESS is represented by either its before-state followed by CRASH or its complete after-state followed by CRASH; a partial E/D write is excluded by premise. The sent request IDs partition disjointly into Q_R, worker IDs in V, and terminal IDs in T. SEND introduces one ID, RECEIVE transfers it, PROCESS changes its worker phase, and enqueue/drop/crash transfers it to T. This proves complete request accounting inductively. Ack IDs similarly partition into Q_A and the delivered/dropped acknowledgment events in J. No automatic redelivery occurs after a pre-commit crash in this model; durable lease/redelivery semantics would be a different model.\", \"epistemic_status\": \"deduction\", \"basis_artifact_ids\": []}, {\"title\": \"Durable invariant and ledger abbreviations\", \"argument\": \"For each key, invariant I is: either D[k] is absent and E contains no effect for k, or D[k]=(p,r,id) and E contains exactly one effect for k, namely (id,k,p), whose recorded result is r. Define Z=(E=empty,D=empty). Define P_x=(E={e_x},D[k]=(p,r_x,id_x)), with e_x=(id_x,k,p) created by delivery x. Define O_b=(E={e_b},D=empty) and O_ba=(E={e_b,e_a},D=empty) for the ordinary control. Z and every P_x satisfy I, including full payload and identifier correspondence, not just counts. O_b and O_ba fail I because ordinary mode intentionally has no D record; O_b still has at-most-one effect, whereas O_ba does not. In atomic mode, first PROCESS creates one matching pair, replay/rejection preserve it, and every other lifecycle transition leaves E,D unchanged. This proves I from empty initialization despite crashes and concurrent workers. It supplies safety only: loss of every ready worker can leave Z forever.\", \"epistemic_status\": \"deduction\", \"basis_artifact_ids\": [\"4435b6ec-fefc-43a1-8706-a3a6794dbbe5\"]}, {\"title\": \"T5: consumed request lost immediately before commit\", \"argument\": \"All requests below carry the same k,p. Each row is the state after the named event. Every durable state is Z or P_b, so I holds on every row.\\nEvent | Q_R | V | Q_A | T | E/D\\ninitial | - | - | - | - | Z\\nSEND a | a | - | - | - | Z\\nRECEIVE a | - | aR | - | - | Z\\nCRASH before PROCESS | - | - | - | a:L0 | Z\\nRESTART | - | - | - | a:L0 | Z\\ntimeout | - | - | - | a:L0 | Z\\nagent restore | - | - | - | a:L0 | Z\\nSEND retry b | b | - | - | a:L0 | Z\\nRECEIVE b | - | bR | - | a:L0 | Z\\nPROCESS b | - | bC | - | a:L0 | P_b\\nACK_ENQUEUE b | - | - | alpha_b | a:L0,b:F | P_b\\nACK_DELIVER alpha_b | - | - | - | a:L0,b:F | P_b\\nJ records alpha_b as delivered in the last row. Delivery a never reappears; only the new retry b creates the effect. Immediately before the crash, |Q_R|=0 but one unprocessed request still exists in V. Immediately afterward both queued and unprocessed-worker counts are zero. This resolves the earlier ambiguous q=0 notation.\", \"epistemic_status\": \"deduction\", \"basis_artifact_ids\": [\"4435b6ec-fefc-43a1-8706-a3a6794dbbe5\"]}, {\"title\": \"T5 boundary control: crash after commit, before acknowledgment enqueue\", \"argument\": \"This is the other crash boundary mentioned in the prior T5 description. I holds on every row, now using Z or P_a.\\nEvent | Q_R | V | Q_A | T | E/D\\ninitial | - | - | - | - | Z\\nSEND a | a | - | - | - | Z\\nRECEIVE a | - | aR | - | - | Z\\nPROCESS a | - | aC | - | - | P_a\\nCRASH before ACK_ENQUEUE | - | - | - | a:L1 | P_a\\nRESTART | - | - | - | a:L1 | P_a\\ntimeout | - | - | - | a:L1 | P_a\\nagent restore | - | - | - | a:L1 | P_a\\nSEND retry b | b | - | - | a:L1 | P_a\\nRECEIVE b | - | bR | - | a:L1 | P_a\\nPROCESS b, replay | - | bC | - | a:L1 | P_a\\nACK_ENQUEUE b | - | - | alpha_b | a:L1,b:F | P_a\\nACK_DELIVER alpha_b | - | - | - | a:L1,b:F | P_a\\nNo alpha_a was ever enqueued. The acknowledgment alpha_b contains the original r_a,id_a. J records alpha_b delivered. Actual completion survives a's lost reply; a's delivery itself is not reconstructed.\", \"epistemic_status\": \"deduction\", \"basis_artifact_ids\": [\"4435b6ec-fefc-43a1-8706-a3a6794dbbe5\"]}, {\"title\": \"T8: a delayed request remains live through lookup and retry\", \"argument\": \"Use the same event schedule for ordinary and atomic handlers. 'lookup' is a stipulated authoritative read of current effects, not a request added to this operation's Q; its query transport is outside this trace. It does not cancel or fence a. I_A holds on every row. I_O holds exactly on the Z rows and fails afterward by design.\\nEvent | Q_R | V | Q_A | T | ordinary E/D | atomic E/D\\ninitial | - | - | - | - | Z | Z\\nSEND a | a | - | - | - | Z | Z\\nDELAY a | a | - | - | - | Z | Z\\ntimeout | a | - | - | - | Z | Z\\nlookup: no effect | a | - | - | - | Z | Z\\nSEND retry b | a,b | - | - | - | Z | Z\\nRECEIVE b | a | bR | - | - | Z | Z\\nPROCESS b | a | bC | - | - | O_b | P_b\\nACK_ENQUEUE b | a | - | alpha_b | b:F | O_b | P_b\\nACK_DELIVER alpha_b | a | - | - | b:F | O_b | P_b\\nrelease delay a | a | - | - | b:F | O_b | P_b\\nRECEIVE a | - | aR | - | b:F | O_b | P_b\\nPROCESS a | - | aC | - | b:F | O_ba | P_b\\nACK_ENQUEUE a | - | - | alpha_a | a:F,b:F | O_ba | P_b\\nACK_DELIVER alpha_a | - | - | - | a:F,b:F | O_ba | P_b\\nJ records both acknowledgments delivered. Ordinary processing creates a second effect on PROCESS a. Atomic processing treats a as a replay and alpha_a returns r_b,id_b. The lookup was correct when made, yet left a live. Neither timeout nor delivery of alpha_b consumed a.\", \"epistemic_status\": \"deduction\", \"basis_artifact_ids\": [\"4435b6ec-fefc-43a1-8706-a3a6794dbbe5\"]}, {\"title\": \"T12: a received and processed first\", \"argument\": \"Two distinct deliveries have identical k,p. Both are dequeued before either PROCESS, allowing concurrent workers. Processing is serialized in order a,b. I holds on every row.\\nEvent | Q_R | V | Q_A | T | E/D\\ninitial | - | - | - | - | Z\\nSEND a | a | - | - | - | Z\\nSEND b | a,b | - | - | - | Z\\nRECEIVE a | b | aR | - | - | Z\\nRECEIVE b | - | aR,bR | - | - | Z\\nPROCESS a | - | aC,bR | - | - | P_a\\nPROCESS b, replay | - | aC,bC | - | - | P_a\\nACK_ENQUEUE a | - | bC | alpha_a | a:F | P_a\\nACK_ENQUEUE b | - | - | alpha_a,alpha_b | a:F,b:F | P_a\\nACK_DELIVER alpha_a | - | - | alpha_b | a:F,b:F | P_a\\nACK_DELIVER alpha_b | - | - | - | a:F,b:F | P_a\\nBoth acknowledgments carry r_a,id_a; J records both delivered. Dequeuing b while D is absent does not reserve permission to create an effect: its PROCESS tests D after a's serialized commit.\", \"epistemic_status\": \"deduction\", \"basis_artifact_ids\": [\"4435b6ec-fefc-43a1-8706-a3a6794dbbe5\"]}, {\"title\": \"T12: b received and processed first\", \"argument\": \"Reverse delivery and processing order to b,a, retaining the same two sends. I holds on every row.\\nEvent | Q_R | V | Q_A | T | E/D\\ninitial | - | - | - | - | Z\\nSEND a | a | - | - | - | Z\\nSEND b | a,b | - | - | - | Z\\nRECEIVE b | a | bR | - | - | Z\\nRECEIVE a | - | aR,bR | - | - | Z\\nPROCESS b | - | aR,bC | - | - | P_b\\nPROCESS a, replay | - | aC,bC | - | - | P_b\\nACK_ENQUEUE b | - | aC | alpha_b | b:F | P_b\\nACK_ENQUEUE a | - | - | alpha_a,alpha_b | a:F,b:F | P_b\\nACK_DELIVER alpha_b | - | - | alpha_a | a:F,b:F | P_b\\nACK_DELIVER alpha_a | - | - | - | a:F,b:F | P_b\\nBoth acknowledgments carry r_b,id_b; J records both delivered. Receive order need not equal processing order: after both RECEIVE events, the ready-worker state is identical in these tables. Choosing either PROCESS first therefore also covers the crossed receive/processing orders. The unique effect ID may differ across alternative executions; within each execution both replies identify its single effect.\", \"epistemic_status\": \"deduction\", \"basis_artifact_ids\": [\"4435b6ec-fefc-43a1-8706-a3a6794dbbe5\"]}, {\"title\": \"Scope and status of the refinement\", \"argument\": \"The explicit RECEIVE and crash rules address the local lifecycle gap recorded in obligations 041a5bf1f13d8ecadcaa67e9f85d9c6defcf7c0292878c28561d3282ac397e9f, f05f8609355469e012f0af211587c3b08e72540487597f0d788953675e46e7a8, and 99bdafb61848d9f5dafb4c29a1e310392c4262e9a6a896d6054f449a64d45cd9 at the specification level only.
